    • Canonical source. A Donchian/Turtle-style channel breakout confirmed by Wilder's ATR (New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems, 1978) as the volatility-expansion filter.
    • Chosen configuration and why. The stop is structural both sides, overriding the campaign's 4x-ATR config. Take-profit is not structural, so the 3.4x-ATR campaign target applies, but the position also exits early whenever the shorter opposite-channel CLOSE fires, regardless of R-multiple reached. No time-stop is authored. Trailing and slippage follow the campaign defaults (5x ATR from +3R, 5 bp). The asymmetric 10-bar entry / 5-bar exit channel mirrors the Turtle System's own asymmetric entry/exit widths rather than a single shared channel for both.
    • Possible improvement. The strategy already implements the canonical opposite/shorter-channel exit in place of a fixed timer. A further refinement would be to opt this strategy into its own trail_atr_mult (rather than depending on the shared campaign trailing_stop_config), so a wide volatility trail rides an extended trend independently of any future campaign-wide trailing-config change.
    • Compromise. No hard limit — trail_atr_mult is a profile parameter already supported by breakout(); adopting it here is a one-line addition, not a missing capability.

    5.4 volatility_contraction_expansion — profile BO

    • Implementation. L1: squeeze_release = volatility{-1} < percentile(volatility{-252:-2}, 15) and volatility{-1} > volatility{-3} — 20-bar rolling volatility sitting in the lowest ~15th percentile of the trailing year and now turning up; LONG adds close{-1} > highest(high{-10:-2}), SHORT the mirror. L2 breakout(): long_stop_expr=lowest(low{-10:-2}) / short_stop_expr=highest(high{-10:-2}). No take-profit expression, no CLOSE expression, no no_follow_bars. window_size=260 covers the 252-bar percentile lookback. Features: BTCUSDT 5m, volatility(20) (rolling std of close), raw OHLCV high/low/close.
    • Canonical source. Mark Minervini's Volatility Contraction Pattern (Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard, 2013 / Think & Trade Like a Champion).
    • Chosen configuration and why. The stop is structural both sides, overriding the campaign's 4x-ATR config. Take-profit is not structural, so the 3.4x-ATR campaign target applies; the position is otherwise left to trail on the campaign's ATR trailing config. No time-stop is authored, consistent with VCP being an explicitly non-time-boxed swing pattern that can stall across several contraction legs before resolving.
    • Possible improvement. Minervini's own management keeps a structural trailing stop as profit accrues — a rising short/medium moving average or the most recent higher-low swing — rather than a flat volatility-based trail. Adding a rising-EMA or swing-low trailing CLOSE once the position is in profit would bring the exit closer to the source while keeping the existing contraction-low initial stop.
    • Defect — wrong feature timeframe (to fix). The dedicated multi-contraction detector now exists (the VOLATILITY_CONTRACTION indicator: progressively tighter legs plus volume dry-up), so this is no longer a missing feature. But Minervini's VCP is a multi-week base, and the detector runs on the 5m base with segment_period=20×num_segments=3 ≈ 5 hours. Base stays 5m; the fix is to compute volatility_contraction on a 1d bucket forward-filled to 5m (segments measured in daily bars). Separately, the stop lowest(low{-10:-2}) is a generic 10-bar Donchian low, not Minervini's low-of-the-final-tightest-contraction (≈7-8% risk cap) — a secondary refinement.

    5.5 parabolic_sar_reversal — profile TR

    • Implementation. L1: LONG cross_up(close{-2:-1}, sar{-2:-1}) and adx.adx{-1} > 20; SHORT the mirror on cross_down. L2 trend_rider(): long_stop_line_expr=sar{-1} / short_stop_line_expr=sar{-1} — the SAR value is both the initial structural stop (placed at open via SET_ENTRY_LEVELS) and the every-bar trail target, ratcheted tighter every bar and never loosened. trend_rider()'s defaults also apply: break-even move at +1R, pyramiding at +2R (≤2 legs). No take-profit expression. Features: BTCUSDT 5m, SAR (acceleration 0.02, maximum 0.2 — features.sar() defaults), ADX(14).
    • Canonical source. J. Welles Wilder's Parabolic Time/Price System (New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems, 1978), including Wilder's own recommendation to filter entries/exits with ADX above 20-25.
    • Chosen configuration and why. The initial stop is structural (the SAR line at open), overriding the campaign's 4x-ATR config, then trailed onto SAR every bar. Take-profit is not structural, so the 3.4x-ATR campaign target applies alongside the SAR flip and the opposite model signal as exit paths; the campaign's ATR trailing config also runs in parallel with the SAR line-trail. Slippage is 5 bp.
    • Possible improvement. None — the SAR line trail with no time-stop and the ADX>20 entry gate already is the criterious, volatility-adaptive stop-and-reverse mechanic Wilder's system prescribes.
    • Compromise. None — already faithful to the canonical source.

    5.6 choppiness_release — profile BO

    • Implementation. L1: release = chop{-2} > 61.8 and chop{-1} < 50 — choppiness falling from clearly choppy to clearly directional; LONG adds close{-1} > highest(high{-10:-2}), SHORT the mirror. L2 breakout(): no stop or take-profit expression — a pure regime filter paired with a channel break, so the tuned config governs both. long_close_expr/short_close_expr add a regime-rollover CLOSE, chop{-1} > 61.8 — the directional regime the breakout relied on has re-choppied. No no_follow_bars. Features: BTCUSDT 5m, Choppiness Index(14), raw OHLCV high/low/close.
    • Canonical source. The Choppiness Index, created by E.W. Dreiss, using its standard Fibonacci thresholds (38.2 / 61.8) to classify trending versus choppy regimes.
    • Chosen configuration and why. Both stop and take-profit fall back to the campaign's tuned config (4x-ATR stop, 3.4x-ATR target) since the strategy sets no structural level of its own. The regime-rollover CLOSE is already wired, no time-stop is authored, and the campaign's ATR trailing config runs alongside. Slippage is 5 bp.
    • Possible improvement. The Choppiness Index is a regime filter with no source-defined trade exit of its own; the symmetric analog — exit or tighten on a regime reversal — is already implemented as a hard CLOSE. A softer version, partially reducing the position once choppiness first crosses back above the midpoint threshold (e.g. 50) rather than waiting for the full re-choppied threshold (61.8), would give a smoother regime-decay exit closer to that "exit or tighten" symmetry.
    • Compromise. There is no primary Dreiss exit rule to be more faithful to — the index defines regime, not trade management — so any exit mechanism here is necessarily an analogy the codebase supplies, not a canonical reproduction; the current regime-recross CLOSE is already as close an analogy as the source supports.

    5.7 dmi_pullback_continuation — profile PB

    • Implementation. L1: LONG adx.plus_di{-1} > adx.minus_di{-1} and adx.adx{-1} > 25 and low{-1} <= ema20{-1} and close{-1} > ema20{-1} and close{-1} > open{-1} — a directional DMI trend, a pullback bar tagging the 20-EMA, and a bounce-confirmation close; SHORT mirrored on -DI. L2 pullback(): long_stop_expr=low{-1} / short_stop_expr=high{-1} place the stop at the pullback bar's own extreme (Wilder's Extreme Point Rule); long_close_expr=adx.minus_di{-1} > adx.plus_di{-1} / short_close_expr=adx.plus_di{-1} > adx.minus_di{-1} add the DI-crossover exit. Features: BTCUSDT 5m, ADX(14) with +DI/-DI, EMA(20), raw OHLCV high/low/close/open.
    • Canonical source. Wilder's Directional Movement System with the Extreme Point Rule (New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems, 1978).
    • Chosen configuration and why. The stop is structural both sides, overriding the campaign's 4x-ATR config. Take-profit is not structural, so the campaign's 3.4x-ATR target applies, since Wilder's system defines no fixed target — the DI crossover is the canonical exit. Partial is 50% at +2R (pullback()'s default), trailing follows the campaign's ATR config, slippage is 5 bp.
    • Possible improvement. None material — the Extreme Point Rule stop and the DI-crossover CLOSE together already reproduce Wilder's system exactly: signal-based exit, no fixed period, no arbitrary time-stop.
    • Compromise. None — already faithful to the canonical source.

    5.8 regime_switch_hybrid — profile HY

    • Implementation. L1 is four first-match rules. Trend leg LONG fires when the daily Market State reads a confirmed trend out of any mixed zone and the 5m EMA stack agrees: trend_trending{-1} == 1 and mixed_regime{-1} == 0 and ema20{-1} > ema50{-1} and close{-1} > ema50{-1}; SHORT mirrored on ema20 < ema50 and close < ema50. Range leg LONG fires when the daily regime reads ranging (not trending) and RSI(14) recrosses up out of oversold: trend_ranging{-1} == 1 and mixed_regime{-1} == 0 and rsi{-2} < 30 and rsi{-1} > 30; SHORT mirrored on the 70 recross. L2 is regime_hybrid(): a break-even move to entry at +1R, pyramiding up to 2 legs at +2R, and a single regime-rollover CLOSE — mixed_regime{-1} == 1 — shared by both legs rather than a per-leg trend_trending{-1} == 0 / trend_ranging{-1} == 0 split or an RSI recross. regime_hybrid() takes no stop/take-profit expression parameters at all, so no SET_ENTRY_LEVELS rule is ever emitted: structural level — none, the tuned config governs both sides on every entry. Features: base 5m BTCUSDT EMA(20), EMA(50), RSI(14), close; daily (1d, multi-timeframe) Market State columns trend_trending, trend_ranging, mixed_regime with vol_baseline_window=30, stability_window=20, vol_of_vol_window=30 (a roughly one-month calibration, rescaled from the indicator's 5m defaults); no 4h bucket is used by this strategy.
    • Canonical source. Not a single named canonical strategy: a composite of a classic dual-EMA trend-following system and a Wilder-style RSI overbought/oversold fade, gated by a trend/range regime classifier that is the practitioner analog of Markov regime-switching frameworks such as Hamilton's.
    • Chosen configuration and why. Stop_loss_config 4.0x ATR, take_profit_config 3.4x ATR, trailing_stop enabled (3.0 ATR activation, 5.0 ATR distance), 5 bp slippage, default risk-based sizing — the campaign's tuned defaults, unmodified for this strategy. Neither leg has an intrinsic price level of its own: a dual-EMA cross has no canonical stop, and an RSI midline fade has no canonical target, so a tuned, config-driven level is the faithful choice rather than inventing a structural number no source supports. Break-even at +1R and pyramiding at +2R (≤2 legs) come from the trend-rider-style template regime_hybrid() reuses; they fit the trend leg naturally and are applied uniformly to the range leg too, since Layer-1 (not Layer-2) is what decides which sub-policy a given entry belongs to.
    • Possible improvement. Split the regime-rollover CLOSE into a leg-specific condition instead of the shared mixed_regime{-1} == 1: close the trend leg on trend_trending{-1} == 0 and the range leg on trend_ranging{-1} == 0, mirroring each leg's own entry gate. Pair the range leg with an oscillator recross (e.g. rsi{-1} < 50 for a held long) so a range trade that never reaches the opposite extreme still exits on the reversion resolving, not only when the higher-timeframe regime turns mixed.
    • Compromise. The regime-switch composition itself is an engineering construct, not a textbook system — the trend leg's own exit convention (opposite EMA cross) and the range leg's (RSI extreme/midline recross) are each independently documented, but there is no single canonical citation for how the combined hybrid should exit. Any exit choice for the composite as a whole is therefore a reasoned engineering call, not a source citation — a hard limit of the strategy's own design, not something a new feature or rule could close.

    5.9 bollinger_squeeze_breakout — profile BO

    • Implementation. L1: squeeze = bb.bandwidth{-1} < percentile(bb.bandwidth{-252:-2}, 10) — band width in the lowest ~10th percentile of the trailing year; LONG adds close{-1} > bb.upper{-1}, SHORT the mirror on bb.lower. L2 breakout(): long_stop_expr=bb.middle{-1} / short_stop_expr=bb.middle{-1} — a close back through the middle band gives back the edge. No take-profit expression, no CLOSE expression, no no_follow_bars. window_size=260 covers the 252-bar percentile lookback. Features: BTCUSDT 5m, Bollinger Bands (period 20, std-dev 2.0 — features.bollinger() defaults).
    • Canonical source. John Bollinger's BandWidth squeeze (Bollinger on Bollinger Bands, 2001).
    • Chosen configuration and why. The stop is structural at the middle band on both sides, overriding the campaign's 4x-ATR config. Take-profit is not structural, so the campaign's 3.4x-ATR target applies. No time-stop is authored, trailing follows the campaign's ATR config, slippage is 5 bp. Bollinger treats a band tag as informational only, never an exit trigger, and explicitly treats the middle-band close as the "walk is over" signal — exactly what the structural stop implements.
    • Possible improvement. None — the middle-band stop already is Bollinger's own "walk is over" rule, and no generic time-stop is layered on top of it.
    • Defect — wrong feature timeframe (to fix). The squeeze percentile is over bandwidth{-252:-2}, described as "the trailing year", but 252 5-minute bars is ~21 hours — squeezes are ranked against a recent noisy window, not a year. Base stays 5m; the fix is to compute BandWidth and its 252-bar percentile on daily bars (a 1d bucket forward-filled to 5m; needs a daily bandwidth-percentile feature). The middle-band stop itself is faithful.

    5.10 bollinger_keltner_squeeze — profile BO

    • Implementation. L1: squeeze_prev = bb.upper{-2} < kc.upper{-2} and bb.lower{-2} > kc.lower{-2} (Bollinger fully inside Keltner) and released_now = (bb.upper{-1} > kc.upper{-1} or bb.lower{-1} < kc.lower{-1}); LONG adds roc{-1} > 0, SHORT roc{-1} < 0 — the release taken in the direction of momentum. L2 breakout(): no stop expression (falls to tuned config); a single structural take-profit, long_take_profit_expr = market_current_price{-1} + 2 * market_atr{-1} (mirrored -2*ATR short) — there is no second, further ATR target. long_close_expr = roc{-1} < roc{-2} and roc{-2} < roc{-3} (mirrored >) adds a two-consecutive-bar momentum-deceleration CLOSE. Features: BTCUSDT 5m, Bollinger Bands (20, 2.0), Keltner Channel (period 20, ATR period 10, multiplier 2.0 — features.keltner() defaults), ROC(20).
    • Canonical source. John Carter's TTM Squeeze (Mastering the Trade, ch. 11, 2005).
    • Chosen configuration and why. The take-profit is structural (entry ± 2 ATR), overriding the campaign's 3.4x-ATR config; the stop is not structural, so the campaign's 4x-ATR stop applies. The ROC-deceleration CLOSE is already wired as the momentum-fade exit, reproducing Carter's rule of thumb — exiting after two consecutive bars of decelerating momentum in the trade's direction — using ROC direction-change as the available proxy for a dedicated momentum-histogram indicator. No time-stop is authored; trailing follows the campaign's ATR config; slippage is 5 bp.
    • Possible improvement. Carter's TTM Squeeze holds the position for as long as the momentum histogram keeps expanding, with no fixed profit multiple; the ROC-deceleration CLOSE already captures that exit condition. The residual fixed +2 ATR target is a practitioner substitute with no basis in Carter's own rule, and now that the deceleration CLOSE exists it is redundant — dropping the fixed take-profit in favor of letting the deceleration CLOSE alone govern the exit would track the canon more closely.
    • Defect — proxy term to replace (to fix). Carter's trigger is a dedicated momentum histogram (a smoothed linear-regression of price vs a Donchian midline); the code proxies both the entry direction and the deceleration exit with roc(20) sign — a workable but imperfect stand-in. The fix is a dedicated momentum-histogram feature (buildable). Also drop the residual fixed +2 ATR take-profit (see Possible improvement), which has no basis in Carter's rule and is redundant with the deceleration CLOSE.

    5.11 nr7_breakout — profile BO

    • Implementation. L1: nr7 = hl_pct{-1} <= lowest(hl_pct{-7:-1}) — the current bar's high-low range (the materialized hl_pct relative-price column) is the narrowest of the last seven; LONG adds close{-1} > high{-2}, SHORT close{-1} < low{-2}. L2 breakout(): long_stop_expr=low{-1} / short_stop_expr=high{-1} — a move back through the narrow-range bar's own extreme invalidates the break; no_follow_bars=10 is passed explicitly, sized to roughly 1.5x the strategy's own 7-bar lookback — not the generic breakout() default, which is None (no time-stop unless a strategy opts in). Features: BTCUSDT 5m, the hl_pct relative-price column (a materialized per-bar range, not a per-bar high - low expression), raw OHLCV high/low/close.
    • Canonical source. Toby Crabel's NR7 breakout (Day Trading with Short-Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout, 1990).
    • Chosen configuration and why. The stop is structural both sides, overriding the campaign's 4x-ATR config. Take-profit is not structural, so the campaign's 3.4x-ATR target applies, alongside the explicit 10-bar stall-cut CLOSE — the one strategy in this family that keeps an active, strategy-sized time-stop, because Crabel's own pattern is a same-session, one-day hold whose 24/7 analog is a lookback-relative bar count rather than the shared profile default. Trailing follows the campaign's ATR config; slippage is 5 bp.
    • Possible improvement. Crabel's own management trails the stop via ATR or Parabolic SAR once the breakout is confirmed, rather than leaving a static stop at the NR7 bar's extreme for the whole hold. Opting this strategy into its own trail_atr_mult once price has moved favorably would track that recommendation without disturbing the initial invalidation stop.
    • Defect — wrong feature timeframe (to fix). Crabel's NR7 is the narrowest range of the last 7 daily bars; here lowest(hl_pct{-7:-1}) ranks 7 five-minute bars (~35 min), a materially different test — the confirmed exemplar of the family-wide feature-timeframe bug. Base stays 5m; the fix is to compute the narrowest-range-over-7 on daily bars (a 1d bucket forward-filled to 5m; needs a daily rolling narrowest-range feature) and break the narrow day's high/low. The only genuine residual limit is Crabel's intraday one-session hold (no session close in 24/7 crypto), which the 10-bar stall-cut approximates — that part alone is a real limit, the 7-day window is not.

    5.12 pivot_breakout_continuation — profile BO

    • Implementation. L1: vol_surge = volume{-1} > avg(volume{-20:-2}) on the 5m base; LONG close{-1} > pivots.r1{-1} and vol_surge and daily_close{-1} > daily_ema200{-1}; SHORT close{-1} < pivots.s1{-1} and vol_surge and daily_close{-1} < daily_ema200{-1}. L2 breakout(): long_stop_expr=pivots.s1{-1}, short_stop_expr=pivots.r1{-1}, long_take_profit_expr=pivots.r2{-1}, short_take_profit_expr=pivots.s2{-1}. No CLOSE expression, no no_follow_bars. Features: two buckets merged — the 5m base (close, volume_base) and a daily bucket (StrategyFeatureSet(symbol=BTCUSDT, timeframe="1d", base_timeframe="5m")) forward-filled onto the 5m grid, providing classic pivots and EMA(200) on daily close.
    • Canonical source. Classic floor-trader pivot points (CME/CBOT floor-trading practice).
    • Chosen configuration and why. Both stop and take-profit are fully structural, overriding the campaign's tuned config entirely — the stop sits at pivots.s1 for the long and pivots.r1 for the short, the target at pivots.r2/pivots.s2. No time-stop or session force-flat exists anywhere in breakout(); trailing follows the campaign's ATR config; slippage is 5 bp.
    • Possible improvement. The current stop assignment is a confirmed bug: long_stop_expr=pivots.s1 and short_stop_expr=pivots.r1 place a LONG's stop at S1 — a level below the central pivot, far under the breakout — and a SHORT's stop at R1, far above it. Floor-trader convention places the stop just inside the broken level itself: R1 for a long breaking above R1, S1 for a short breaking below S1, so the broken level becomes support/resistance for the stop, not the opposite pivot. The take-profit assignment (R2 for the long, S2 for the short) is correct and needs no change. The approved fix — swapping the two stop expressions to long_stop_expr=pivots.r1{-1} and short_stop_expr=pivots.s1{-1} — has not been applied to the code.
    • Compromise. Floor-trader pivots are computed once per session and are canonically valid only for that session; a position still open when the next daily pivot bar rolls over is trading against stale reference levels. The engine has the pivot feature itself but no explicit "new daily pivot available" or stale-level trigger wired as a CLOSE condition — surmountable with a dedicated pivot-rollover feature, not a hard limit.

    5.13 fractal_breakout_retest — profile PB

    • Implementation. L1: LONG close{-1} > fractals.high_level{-1} and any(low{-3:-1} <= fractals.high_level{-1}) and close{-1} > open{-1} — a close beyond the last confirmed swing-high level, a recent bar that tagged it back (the retest), and a close in the trade direction (the bounce); SHORT mirrored on fractals.low_level. L2 pullback(): long_stop_expr=fractals.low_level{-1} / short_stop_expr=fractals.high_level{-1} — the nearest opposing fractal level. No take-profit expression, no CLOSE expression (pullback() has no time_stop_bars parameter at all, so no time-stop is possible under this profile). Features: BTCUSDT 5m, Fractals (window 5 — features.fractals() default) emitting swing flags plus carried-forward high_level/low_level swing prices, raw OHLCV high/low/close/open.
    • Canonical source. Bill Williams' Fractals within the Profitunity/Chaos system (Trading Chaos, 1995).
    • Chosen configuration and why. The stop is structural both sides (the nearest opposing fractal), overriding the campaign's 4x-ATR config. Take-profit is not structural, so the campaign's 3.4x-ATR target applies; partial is 50% at +2R (pullback()'s default); no time-stop exists (mechanically unavailable under this profile). Trailing follows the campaign's ATR config; slippage is 5 bp.
    • Possible improvement. Williams ties his exits to the Alligator indicator's jaw/teeth/lips alignment — a converging or crossing Alligator signals trend exhaustion — rather than only the opposing-fractal stop already in place. Adding a CLOSE/tighten rule on the Alligator lines converging or crossing, once available, would supply the second canonical trigger alongside the existing fractal-level stop.
    • Compromise. The Alligator indicator (three smoothed, forward-displaced moving averages, typically 13/8/5 periods) does not exist in the feature helpers yet, so the strategy currently substitutes the opposing-fractal-level stop as an incomplete proxy for the full Williams exit rule. Surmountable — it needs a new feature to build, not a hard limit.

    6. Regime family

    6.1 regime_confirmed_trend — profile TR

    • Implementation. L1 LONG fires when the daily Market State reads a confirmed, established uptrend — trend_trending{-1} == 1 and dir_bullish{-1} == 1 and mixed_regime{-1} == 0 and bars_since_regime_change_count{-1} > 5 (more than 5 days since the daily regime last changed) — the 4h regime agrees on direction (dir_bullish{-1} == 1), and the 5m EMA(20)/EMA(50) stack confirms with price above the slow EMA: ema20{-1} > ema50{-1} and close{-1} > ema50{-1}. SHORT mirrors every term on the bearish side. L2 is trend_rider() with no stop/take-profit expression passed (structural level — none, the tuned config governs both sides), a break-even move to entry at +1R, pyramiding up to 2 legs at +2R, and a regime-rollover CLOSE that mirrors the entry gate exactly: for a held long, trend_trending{-1} == 0 or mixed_regime{-1} == 1 or dir_bearish{-1} (4h) == 1; short mirrored on the 4h dir_bullish. Features: base 5m BTCUSDT EMA(20), EMA(50), close; daily (1d) Market State columns trend_trending, dir_bullish, dir_bearish, mixed_regime, bars_since_regime_change_count with vol_baseline_window=30, stability_window=20, vol_of_vol_window=30; 4h Market State columns dir_bullish, dir_bearish with vol_baseline_window=42, stability_window=42, vol_of_vol_window=50 — roughly a one-week calibration on the 4h bucket against a one-month calibration on the daily one.
    • Canonical source. Alexander Elder's Triple Screen Trading System (Trading for a Living, 1993), rescaled onto this engine's three timeframes: the daily regime stands in for Elder's tide, the 4h regime for the wave, and the 5m EMA20/EMA50 stack for the ripple entry timing.
    • Chosen configuration and why. Stop_loss_config 4.0x ATR, take_profit_config 3.4x ATR, trailing_stop enabled (3.0 ATR activation, 5.0 ATR distance), 5 bp slippage, default risk-based sizing. Elder's own Triple Screen, and the broader ADX/Kaufman trend-confirmation literature it sits alongside, treat the stop as a trailing/money-management overlay rather than a price derived from the trend/regime features themselves — there is no structural level to author here, so the tuned config plus the trailing overlay is the faithful choice. Break-even at +1R and pyramiding at +2R are R-multiple, not time-based, matching the canon's own intent of riding the tide for as long as it holds.
    • Possible improvement. None of substance beyond what is already implemented: the regime-rollover CLOSE reads exactly the daily/4h features the entry gates on (trend_trending, mixed_regime, the 4h dir_bullish/dir_bearish), so the exit is already as adaptive to each symbol's own regime persistence as the entry, with no fixed bar count anywhere in the strategy's definition.
    • Compromise. Elder's canon holds a position for as long as the daily-chart tide stays intact, which in his own setup runs days to weeks; rescaled onto a daily tide read against 5m bars, the analogous hold is however long the daily regime stays a confirmed, non-mixed trend in the trade's direction — often hundreds to low thousands of 5m bars. That rescaled horizon cannot be checked against Elder's own numbers, because his tide was itself computed on daily bars, not derived from a faster timeframe; treating the rescaling as faithful is a reasoned analogy, not a quoted figure — a hard limit of adapting a multi-day equity system onto continuous 5m crypto, not something an added rule could resolve.

    7. Session family

    7.1 vwap_continuation — profile IN

    • Implementation. L1 LONG fires when close sits above the day-anchored VWAP but the bar's low tagged the VWAP and the bar closed bullish: close{-1} > vwap{-1} and low{-1} <= vwap{-1} and close{-1} > open{-1}; SHORT mirrors every term (close{-1} < vwap{-1} and high{-1} >= vwap{-1} and close{-1} < open{-1}). L2 is intraday(): a structural stop at the extreme of the bar that held VWAP — low{-1} long / high{-1} short, set via SET_ENTRY_LEVELS — with no structural take-profit, so the target falls back to the tuned config; a 50% partial at +1R; and a CLOSE the instant price closes back through VWAP against the position (close{-1} < vwap{-1} for a held long, close{-1} > vwap{-1} for a held short) — the level flipping from support to resistance or vice versa. Because BTCUSDT trades continuously, intraday() never emits a clock-based force-flat here or in any strategy built on it — there is no session close on a 24/7 instrument to flatten against. Features: base 5m BTCUSDT VWAP (day-anchored), high, low, close, open — no higher-timeframe context.
    • Canonical source. Brian Shannon's Anchored VWAP method (Maximum Trading Gains With Anchored VWAP; summarized at alphatrends.net).
    • Chosen configuration and why. The stop is structural — the bar that held VWAP — because Shannon's own framing is that the level itself, not a generic distance, is what lets a trader "cut our losers, hold our winners"; a fixed-distance stop would discard the exact information the strategy trades on. The target stays on the tuned take_profit_config (3.4x ATR) because Shannon applies anchored VWAP across day traders, swing traders and investors alike with no inherent duration or distance cap in the method — there is no structural target to author, and the VWAP-flip CLOSE is the real canonical exit, with the config take-profit only a secondary backstop. Trailing stays on the tuned config (3.0 ATR activation, 5.0 ATR distance); slippage 5 bp.
    • Possible improvement. None needed on the exit side — the VWAP-flip CLOSE and the bar-extreme stop already match the canon's own management framing, with no clock retrofit anywhere. A no-follow-through filter for a pullback that neither continues nor stops out could be added, but it should be sized to the pullback's own span rather than a shared bar count, and the canon does not require it.
    • Compromise. Shannon's method assumes a market with a session open/close, since day traders re-anchor the VWAP each session; BTCUSDT trades continuously, so "session" here means the calendar day the VWAP resets on, not a market session with a natural flat point. This is already resolved rather than an open gap: anchoring VWAP to the day (instead of a trading session) and dropping any clock-based flat carries the level-based entry/exit logic over intact — nothing about a 24/7 instrument works against the strategy's actual mechanic.

    7.2 vwap_reversion — profile IN

    • Implementation. L1 LONG fires when close closes beyond the lower VWAP standard-deviation band and the bar turns bullish: close{-1} < vwap_bands.lower{-1} and close{-1} > open{-1}, where the bands are the day-anchored VWAP ± 2 volume-weighted standard deviations (vwap_bands(anchor="DAY", std_dev=2.0)); SHORT mirrors on the upper band. L2 is intraday(): a structural take-profit at the VWAP-bands middle line for both sides (vwap_bands.middle{-1}, computed identically to the anchored VWAP itself); a structural stop ~1 ATR beyond entry — market_current_price{-1} - market_atr{-1} long / + market_atr{-1} short, reading the engine's always-available current-price/ATR context fields rather than a declared indicator; a 50% partial at +1R; and a stretch-relative stall CLOSE — position_bars_since_entry{-1} >= 2.5 * (abs(position_entry_price{-1} - position_initial_take_profit{-1}) / market_atr{-1}) — that scales the cutoff to how far price was stretched from VWAP at entry relative to ATR, rather than a flat bar count. As with every intraday() strategy on this 24/7 instrument, there is no clock-based force-flat. Features: base 5m BTCUSDT VWAP_BANDS (day-anchored, 2 sigma), close, open — no ATR indicator is declared; the stop reads the engine's built-in market_atr context field directly.
    • Canonical source. VWAP standard-deviation band fade practice (bookmap.com, SMB) for the entry and stop; the target-at-VWAP convention is the same anchored-VWAP mean-reversion idea documented across practitioner VWAP-fade references (crosstrade.io, HorizonAI).
    • Chosen configuration and why. Entry, target and stop are all structural rather than tuned-config, because the strategy's own canon defines both a mean to revert to (VWAP, via the bands' middle line) and a stop distance relative to the stretch that triggered the fade (~1x ATR beyond the trigger, per crosstrade.io's documented VWAP-reversion stop rule) — using the tuned config for either would substitute an arbitrary number for a level the canon actually specifies. The k=2.5 stall multiplier sits inside the documented k≈2-3 guidance for abandoning a reversion that has not started moving, and it shrinks the cutoff for a mild stretch and grows it for a violent one, per symbol and timeframe, instead of a flat bar count. The tuned trailing config (3.0 ATR activation, 5.0 ATR distance) still applies as a secondary overlay once the position is open; slippage 5 bp.
    • Possible improvement. Capture the ATR value at entry and use it in the stall-cut formula instead of the live market_atr. The position-context fields the engine exposes today (position_entry_price, position_initial_take_profit, position_bars_since_entry, position_r_multiple) do not include an entry-time ATR snapshot, so the stall threshold recomputes against the current bar's ATR, which drifts if volatility changes materially during the hold; an entry-time snapshot would keep the stretch-over-ATR ratio stable for the life of the trade instead of a moving target.
    • Compromise. An entry-time ATR snapshot does not exist in the engine's position context, so the exact formula the canon implies — stretch at entry over ATR at entry — is only approximable with the live ATR, not literally reproducible, without adding that field. This is surmountable: a small addition to the position-context fields the action-rule DSL already reads would close it, but it is not achievable with the primitives available today.

    8. Cross-asset family (base ETHUSDT, context BTCUSDT)

    8.1 dual_momentum — profile TR

    • Implementation. L1: LONG base_mom{-1} > 0 and base_fast{-1} > 0 and base_mom{-1} > context_mom{-1}; SHORT mirrored base_mom{-1} < 0 and base_fast{-1} < 0 and base_mom{-1} < context_mom{-1}, where base_mom = ETHUSDT roc(365), base_fast = ETHUSDT roc(90), context_mom = BTCUSDT roc(365), all on the daily (1d) bucket forward-filled onto the 5m grid (the strategy's own trading/management granularity stays 5m). L2: trend_rider() called with only long_close_expr / short_close_expr set — no stop_expr or stop_line_expr, so _set_entry_levels() emits no SET_ENTRY_LEVELS rule and stop/ take-profit fall through entirely to the tuned numeric config. It emits an explicit CLOSE pair — long base_mom{-1} <= 0 or base_mom{-1} <= context_mom{-1}, short mirrored — plus the profile defaults: break-even move at +1R and a pyramid add at +2R capped at 2 legs; no ATR trailing overlay (trailing is off by default, governed by the tuned trailing_stop_config if it fires). Structural level: none — tuned config governs. Features: two merged StrategyFeatureSet buckets, ETHUSDT@1d (roc(365), roc(90)) and BTCUSDT@1d (roc(365)), both MTF-grouped and aligned onto the 5m grid.
    • Canonical source. Gary Antonacci's Dual Momentum (Global Equities Momentum) grounds the absolute-plus-relative gating logic, but Antonacci's own GEM uses a single 12-month lookback with deliberately no shorter confirmation leg — he prefers 12 months alone to cut trading frequency and for tax efficiency. The 90-day confirm leg is therefore not attributable to Antonacci; it is attributed to the broader 3/6/12-month academic momentum literature and to Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012, Time Series Momentum), whose own tested lookback/holding grid spans 1–12 months and is explicitly robust across that range, validating both the 90-day and 365-day legs. The crypto-specific caveat is that Palazzi (2025) finds the empirically optimal Bitcoin momentum window sits around 125–230 days — shorter than the traditional 365-day equity/futures anchor, though 365 remains defensible as the cross-asset canonical horizon and sits inside MOP's own tested range.
    • Chosen configuration and why. Stop and take-profit come from the campaign-wide tuned config (ATR-based stop at 4.0×ATR, ATR-based take-profit at 3.4×ATR, trailing stop at 3.0×ATR activation / 5.0×ATR distance), position sizing is volatility_target at a 0.5% (target_volatility_fraction = 0.005) equity fraction (size = target_volatility_fraction * equity / atr), and slippage is modeled at 5 bp (estimated_slippage = 0.0005). GEM itself carries no per-trade stop — it exits only on the periodic momentum-sign re-evaluation — so the numeric ATR stop is a deliberate bound on intraday risk for a signal that the canon only re-checks monthly but this engine re-checks every 5m bar; the explicit sign-flip CLOSE pair already mirrors the canonical exit directly, so risk is bounded by two independent mechanisms (the config stop and the momentum flip) rather than by the stop alone. Volatility-target sizing keeps each position's risk contribution comparable regardless of which side of the pair is currently favored, in the same spirit as GEM equalizing exposure across legs.
    • Possible improvement. Shift the absolute-momentum leg toward the empirically optimal ~125–230-day crypto window from Palazzi (2025) — e.g. testing a 180–230-day leg alongside the existing 90-day confirm — instead of the traditional 365-day equity anchor, and pair it with a decision-cadence gate that only re-evaluates the signal on a new daily bar close rather than every 5m bar, closer to Antonacci's monthly rebalance cadence and less prone to whipsaw on a slow signal sampled too often.
    • Compromise. Antonacci's design holds a single leg for a full month with no intraday stop; on this engine the same signal is re-checked every 5m bar and still carries a numeric ATR stop/target, so the "no stop, monthly hold" governance itself is not fully replicated. This is surmountable — it needs a decision-cadence gate to author, not a new engine primitive — but it is not implemented today.

    8.2 relative_strength_leader — profile TR

    • Implementation. L1: LONG base_mom{-1} > context_mom{-1}; SHORT mirrored base_mom{-1} < context_mom{-1}, where base_mom = ETHUSDT roc(180) and context_mom = BTCUSDT roc(180), both on the daily (1d) bucket aligned onto the 5m grid. There is no spread-widening confirmation term: a daily return is a step function that does not change within a day, so comparing it across a 5-bar (25-minute) offset on the 5m grid would be meaningless — the entry is simply the base outperforming the context over the lookback. L2: trend_rider() called with only long_close_expr / short_close_expr set — no stop expression, so no SET_ENTRY_LEVELS rule is emitted and stop/take-profit fall through to the tuned config. Explicit CLOSE pair — long base_mom{-1} <= context_mom{-1}, short mirrored — plus the profile defaults: break-even at +1R, pyramid add at +2R capped at 2 legs, no ATR trail. Structural level: none — tuned config governs. Features: ETHUSDT@1d roc(180) merged with BTCUSDT@1d roc(180), both MTF-grouped and aligned onto the 5m grid; strategy base timeframe stays 5m.
    • Canonical source. The relative-strength rotation lineage: Levy (1967), "Relative Strength as a Criterion for Investment Selection," and Faber (2010), "Relative Strength Strategies for Investing" — rank the universe by trailing return and hold the leader until it loses rank. Here the "universe" is reduced to a single base/context pair rather than Levy's or Faber's full cross-sectional ranking.
    • Chosen configuration and why. Same campaign tuned stop/take-profit/trailing (4.0×ATR / 3.4×ATR / 3.0×ATR activation with 5.0×ATR trailing distance), volatility_target sizing at a 0.5% (target_volatility_fraction = 0.005) equity fraction, and 5 bp modeled slippage. Pure relative-strength rotation carries no per-position stop in the canon — the only governing exit is the rank/spread reversing — so the tuned ATR stop and the explicit RS-reversal CLOSE together give two independent exits without contradicting the ranking logic; volatility-target sizing keeps risk comparable whichever side of the pair currently leads.
    • Possible improvement. The 180-day lookback already sits inside/near the empirically optimal ~125–230-day crypto momentum window (Palazzi, 2025), so that leg needs no change. The better-grounded improvement is widening the ranking from a single base/context pair to Levy's/Faber's actual multi-asset universe rank-and-hold (more context symbols, trade the top-ranked one), and optionally stacking Faber's slow trend overlay (a long SMA filter), which several published variants add as an extra invalidation on top of the rank.
    • Compromise. A two-asset pair cannot replicate a genuine cross-sectional ranking — Levy and Faber compare many assets and rotate capital into the top-N. With only ETHUSDT and BTCUSDT wired as base and context, this strategy is a leader/laggard pair test, not a rotation. It is surmountable — it needs more context symbols and a ranking rule, not a new engine primitive — but it is not implemented today.
    • Defect — missing canonical term (to fix). The canon (research row #17) is rel_strength_vs_ctx{-1} > rel_strength_vs_ctx{-20} and close{-1} > ema_50{-1}. Two gaps: (1) the close > ema_50 trend filter is absent from the code with no disclosure; (2) the relative-strength widening term (rel_strength{-1} > rel_strength{-20}) was dropped as "meaningless across a 25-min offset" — but that reasoning is itself the feature-timeframe bug: {-20} should be 20 daily bars, which is meaningful. Base stays 5m; the fix is to add the close > ema_50 filter and restore the widening term computed over daily bars (a 1d bucket forward-filled to 5m).

    8.3 context_risk_on — profile TR

    • Implementation. L1: risk_on = context_close{-1} > context_ema200{-1}, risk_off the mirrored <, where context_close and context_ema200 are BTCUSDT close and ema(200) on the daily (1d) bucket aligned onto the 5m grid. LONG: risk_on and ema_fast{-1} > ema_slow{-1} and close{-1} > ema_slow{-1}; SHORT: risk_off and ema_fast{-1} < ema_slow{-1} and close{-1} < ema_slow{-1}, where ema_fast = ETHUSDT ema(20), ema_slow = ETHUSDT ema(50), and close is the ETHUSDT close, all on the base 5m timeframe. L2: trend_rider() called with only long_close_expr / short_close_expr set — no stop expression, so stop/take-profit fall through to the tuned config. Explicit CLOSE pair — long ema_fast{-1} < ema_slow{-1} or context_close{-1} < context_ema200{-1}, short mirrored — plus the profile defaults: break-even at +1R, pyramid add at +2R capped at 2 legs, no ATR trail. Structural level: none — tuned config governs. Features: ETHUSDT@5m ema(20), ema(50), close; BTCUSDT@1d close and ema(200), MTF-grouped and aligned onto the 5m grid.
    • Canonical source. Mebane Faber, "A Quantitative Approach to Tactical Asset Allocation" — a slow ~10-month simple-moving-average (~200-day) regime filter that flips only a handful of times a year, here nested with a faster tactical trend read (the base's own EMA20/50 stack) that governs entries and exits inside the slow regime.
    • Chosen configuration and why. Same campaign tuned stop/take-profit/trailing (4.0×ATR / 3.4×ATR / 3.0×ATR activation with 5.0×ATR trailing distance), volatility_target sizing at a 0.5% (target_volatility_fraction = 0.005) equity fraction, and 5 bp modeled slippage. The regime filter itself carries no per-trade stop — it exits to cash on the SMA/EMA flip — so the numeric stop/target and the trailing overlay bound the nested tactical leg's own risk, while the explicit either-condition CLOSE already captures both nested invalidations (base structure break, or context regime flip) exactly as Faber's crossover exit intends.
    • Possible improvement. Match Faber's literal filter — a simple moving average (the published ~10-month SMA) rather than an EMA200 on the context symbol, since his rule and its documented track record are specifically SMA-based — and/or broaden the regime gate to a wider risk-on basket (more than one context symbol) the way Faber's tactical allocation model rotates across an asset universe rather than a single BTC/ETH pair.
    • Compromise. The nested-condition structure already matches Faber's structural exit faithfully; what remains unfaithful is scope — Faber's tactical allocation model is a multi-asset rotation under one regime signal, while this strategy pairs exactly one base against one context symbol. This is surmountable with more context features and a ranking/rotation rule, not a hard engine limit.
    • Defect — missing canonical term (to fix). The canon (research row #26) is base_signal_trend{-1} == 1 and ctx_market_risk_on{-1} == 1 and ctx_vol_regime_bad{-1} == 0. The third term — the context symbol's bad-volatility-regime filter (ctx_vol_regime_bad == 0) — is absent from the code with no disclosure; only the base trend and the context risk-on terms are implemented. The fix is to add the context vol-regime filter (the context symbol's Market State vol-regime column). Separately, Faber's filter is a ~10-month SMA, not the EMA(200) used here (already noted under Possible improvement).

    9. Notes and caveats

    • Sizing interaction. A structural stop is often tighter or wider than the tuned default, so it changes the per-trade risk distance and therefore risk-based position size. This is intended — the stop reflects the strategy's own invalidation level rather than a one-size default.
    • Time-based exits are not generic profile defaults. The breakout() profile emits no time-stop unless one is explicitly requested (no_follow_bars defaults to off); only nr7_breakout sets one, sized to its own 7-bar lookback (10 bars). The mean_reversion() and failure_reversal() profiles carry a per-strategy time_stop_bars tuned to that strategy's target/band window (20–30 bars), not a shared constant. No clock-based force-flat exists anywhere — the market is 24/7. The exit-code evidence in §11 is the reason: arbitrary time exits historically closed trades at a near-zero win rate.
    • Source confidence. Most stop/target rules map to a named primary source at high or medium confidence. Two cases rest on weaker ground and are flagged in their entries: distance_from_ema_reversion uses a 1.5·ATR stop that no named source prescribes (documented envelope-reversion conventions use a wider 2–3·ATR stop or a wider percentage band), and volatility_contraction_expansion uses a generic opposite-channel stop rather than the tighter final-contraction stop the VCP source defines.

    10. Fidelity — canonical vs compromise

    How faithful each strategy is to its canonical source, and what (if anything) still stands between it and a fully faithful implementation. Gaps fall into four kinds.

    10.1 Faithful — canonical entry, level and exit all in place

    The majority. Each carries its canonical entry, its structural stop/target where the source defines one, and an explicit CLOSE on the source's own exit condition (opposite channel, DI reversal, oscillator/zero-line recross, signal-line cross, momentum-sign flip, regime-flag flip, VWAP flip). The cleanest are supertrend_flip and parabolic_sar_reversal — the indicator line is the trailing stop, exactly the canonical stop-and-reverse mechanic.

    10.2 Compromise — an exit threshold looser than the source

    A small set exits correctly in kind but at a looser threshold than the named source, recorded per entry: rsi_range_reversal, cci_extreme_reversal and mfi_exhaustion_reversal exit on the oscillator midline rather than the opposite extreme the source defines (a switch to the opposite extreme — RSI 70/30, CCI ±100, MFI 90/10 — is listed as pending in §13). distance_from_ema_reversion uses a 1.5·ATR stop with no named-source backing.

    10.3 Gap — a missing feature (a new indicator column)

    The features previously missing here are now built and wired: the Alligator exit (fractal_breakout_retest), the z-score half-life estimator (zscore_reversion_to_mean), the volume distribution-day count (volume_impulse_breakout), the VCP multi-contraction detector (volatility_contraction_expansion), the daily pivot-rollover flag (SESSION_BAR, pivot_breakout_continuation), and the entry-time ATR snapshot exposed to the DSL as position_entry_atr (vwap_reversion). The regression-channel and VWAP standard-deviation bands are likewise built and in use.

    The features still missing are the higher-timeframe (daily) columns the feature-timeframe defects need (see §13.B), since a rolling window over the 5m grid cannot span days: a daily high/low channel (donchian_breakout, turtle_breakout, failed_breakout_reversal), a daily narrowest-range flag (nr7_breakout), a daily directional-bar count (consecutive_bar_exhaustion), a daily inside-bar pattern (inside_bar_expansion), a daily BandWidth-percentile (bollinger_squeeze_breakout), and a momentum-histogram (bollinger_keltner_squeeze). sma_regime_cross and ichimoku_cloud_breakout need no new feature — their existing SMA/Ichimoku indicators run on the 1d bucket directly.

    10.4 Gap — authoring / design choice (horizon, cadence, sizing)

    The momentum and cross-asset family (time_series_momentum, multi_horizon_momentum, mtf_momentum_stack, dual_momentum, relative_strength_leader, context_risk_on) declares a long horizon by reading the daily (1d) bucket aligned onto the 5m grid — roc(90/180/365) ≈ 3/6/12 months — and sizes by volatility target rather than risk-based, matching the canon's equal-volatility positions. The mapping is grounded in Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen's Time Series Momentum (robust across 1–12-month lookbacks); crypto-specific work (Palazzi, 2025) puts the empirically strongest BTC window nearer 125–230 days, a caveat on the 12-month leg. One choice remains open: cadence and intraday firing. These daily-only signals carry no base-5m term, so on the 5m grid the daily value is constant all day and the entry condition is true on every 5m bar — the strategy would enter at the day's first bar and re-enter after any intraday stop, all day. The pure-HTF cases are time_series_momentum, multi_horizon_momentum, dual_momentum and relative_strength_leader; mtf_momentum_stack, context_risk_on and regime_confirmed_trend are milder (they carry a 5m term, but it is a slow state, not a per-bar event). Two authoring options, to be built as two variants of each affected strategy and compared:

    • V1 — decide on the daily bar. A decision-cadence gate evaluates the signal only when a new daily bar closes — on the just-completed daily bar (no lookahead), acting on the next 5m bar, which is the new day's open — so the strategy re-decides once per day (matching the canon's slow cadence) while the base timeframe stays 5m: one entry per daily signal, no intraday re-entry.
    • V2 — daily bias at the open + a 5m trigger. The daily signal sets the day's directional bias at the daily bar's open; the actual entry then waits for a strategy-specific 5m event (a fractal trigger) rather than firing on the bias alone — e.g. a 5m pullback-and-resume toward a fast 5m MA in the bias direction, or a 5m momentum/price cross in the bias direction. This keeps the strategy genuinely intraday-executed on the 5m base and gives a defined entry bar.

    Either option keeps the base timeframe at 5m; changing the base timeframe to 1d for these is the fallback only if neither variant proves workable.

    10.5 Entry mechanics adapted (faithful in spirit, simplified in the trigger)

    Five strategies keep a faithful level/exit but simplify the canonical entry: adx_di_surge (drops Wilder's "hold beyond the signal-bar extreme" confirmation), dmi_pullback_continuation (a continuation entry rather than Wilder's DI-cross entry), fractal_breakout_retest (close+retest rather than a stop-order beyond the fractal with an Alligator filter), nr7_breakout (close beyond the prior bar rather than Crabel's opening-range stretch order), consecutive_bar_exhaustion (a Keltner-extreme gate rather than Connors' 200-period MA filter). Each is a deliberate, mostly-cheap simplification, not an engine limit.

    With the spread/pairs z-score reversion not among the 51 (it needs two-leg coordinated execution), no hard structural engine limit remains among the 51 — every open compromise is a rule to author, a feature to build (§10.3), or a horizon/cadence choice.

    11. Holding time and exit timing

    The single most damaging finding of the executed campaign is that arbitrary time-based exits closed the most trades at a near-total loss. Exit-code breakdown of the 63,605 closed trades of the executed rule_lab_catalog_2024 campaign (50 full backtests):

    Exit code Trades Total PnL Avg hold Win rate
    TAKE_PROFIT 13,313 +$156,793 237 min 97%
    REDUCE 6,175 +$7,210 390 min 100%
    TRAILING_STOP 2,156 −$11,256 413 min 0%
    FLAT_AT_TIME (20:00 UTC) 2,909 −$6,691 45 min 10%
    STOP_LOSS 19,241 −$221,258 178 min 0%
    RULE_EXIT (profile time-stops) 19,811 −$76,424 66 min 0.16%

    The two arbitrary time exits — the fixed bar-count time-stops (RULE_EXIT) and the 20:00 UTC session force-flat (FLAT_AT_TIME) — together closed 22,720 trades for −$83,115 at a near-zero win rate. The time-stops in particular cut trades at ~66 minutes almost always at a loss (0.16% win): they guillotine positions long before the thesis can play out.

    11.1 What the canon says about holding time

    Across all 51 strategies the research is nearly unanimous:

    • A session force-flat does not belong on 24/7 crypto. Of the 51, zero have a canonical basis for a session-close flat — crypto has no session close. The 20:00 UTC flat is an equities concept imported by mistake and is removed for all strategies. (Genuinely intraday-VWAP strategies still exit on their stop / VWAP target / opposite signal, just not on a clock.)
    • Fixed bar-count time-stops are not part of almost any canonical definition. The classical systems end a trade on a condition — the opposite channel/signal/oscillator recross, or a volatility stop — not on a timer. The fixed 6 / 24 / 8-bar cutoffs were bolted on "by eye" and are disconnected from each strategy's own lookback.

    11.2 The adaptable principle (replacing the fixed timers)

    Instead of a fixed bar count, exit timing should follow, in order of preference:

    1. The strategy's own canonical exit condition, authored as an explicit CLOSE (§10.2) — self-adapting, because it lasts exactly as long as the setup holds.
    2. The structural stop (wired in this catalog) as the hard invalidation floor.
    3. Only if a stall cutoff is still wanted, make it relative to the strategy's own window and to volatility, not a shared constant — e.g. a breakout with a 15-bar lookback cuts at ~a fraction/multiple of 15 bars; a mean-reversion trade cuts at a multiple of its band/z-score window or of its estimated mean-reversion half-life (ATR- and lookback-scaled), which adapts automatically per symbol and timeframe.

    The per-strategy detail below records, for each strategy, what its source says about holding horizon, what governs its exit, and the criterious recommendation on 24/7 crypto at a 5m timeframe.

    13. Change status

    Where the catalog stands: what is in force, what is proposed and not yet applied, what is a standing compromise, which choices approximate a canon that does not map cleanly to 24/7 5m crypto, and what remains.

    13.A In force

    • Structural stop/target levels on every strategy whose source defines one (broken-channel stops, band middles, reversion means, indicator-line stops, pivot/fractal levels, swing extremes).
    • Explicit canonical CLOSE rules across the catalog (opposite channel, DI reversal, oscillator/zero-line recross, signal-line cross, momentum-sign flip, regime-flag flip, VWAP flip), instead of relying on the slower implicit opposite-entry flip.
    • No clock-based force-flat anywhere — an equities artifact with no basis on a 24/7 market.
    • Per-strategy stall cuts where kept are sized to the strategy's own lookback/window, not a shared constant.
    • Daily horizon on the momentum/cross-asset family (roc on the 1d bucket ≈ 3/6/12 months) and volatility-target sizing on those six.
    • Regression-channel bands and VWAP standard-deviation bands built and wired into linreg_slope_breakout and vwap_reversion.
    • Costs: 5 bp/side slippage, calibrated against a BTCUSDT execution-cost audit.

    13.B Proposed and pending (not yet applied)

    • pivot_breakout_continuation stop swap — confirmed level error: a long breaking above R1 is stopped at S1 (far below the pivot) and a short breaking below S1 at R1; the canon (and the function's own comment) place the stop just inside the broken level. Fix: long_stop_expr → R1, short_stop_expr → S1 (targets R2/S2 already correct).
    • Oscillator exits to the opposite extreme — switch rsi_range_reversal, cci_extreme_reversal and mfi_exhaustion_reversal from the midline recross to the opposite extreme (RSI 70/30, CCI ±100, MFI 90/10), matching the named sources. williams_reversal (−50 is a documented Williams convention), stochastic_reversal (opposite %K/%D cross) and rsi2_dip_buy (5-bar-average, Connors) stay as they are.
    • Optional stop re-grounding — distance_from_ema_reversion's 1.5·ATR stop → a sourced 2–3·ATR or a wider percentage band; volatility_contraction_expansion's opposite-channel stop → a tighter final-contraction stop.
    • Feature-timeframe fixes — ten strategies compute a canonically daily/weekly pattern on the 5m base, collapsing the lookback to hours (per-entry "Defect" notes). Recompute each pattern's feature on the 1d bucket forward-filled onto the 5m grid — the base timeframe stays 5m — building the daily feature columns listed in §10.3: nr7_breakout, donchian_breakout, turtle_breakout, failed_breakout_reversal, inside_bar_expansion, consecutive_bar_exhaustion, bollinger_squeeze_breakout, volatility_contraction_expansion, plus sma_regime_cross and ichimoku_cloud_breakout (daily-bucket SMA / Ichimoku, no new feature). The daily pattern is the context; the entry trigger stays a 5m event — the 5m close crossing the daily level (cross_up/cross_down), not a static comparison against a value that is constant all day (see §10.4) — so these do not fire all day.
    • Missing canonical terms — relative_strength_leader: add the close > ema_50 trend filter and restore the relative-strength widening term computed over daily bars. context_risk_on: add the ctx_vol_regime_bad == 0 context volatility-regime filter. bollinger_keltner_squeeze: replace the roc momentum proxy with a momentum-histogram feature and drop the residual +2 ATR target.

    13.C Compromises — what cannot be made fully faithful

    • spread/pairs z-score reversion — not among the 51; needs coordinated two-leg execution the single-instrument engine does not support.
    • Pure-oscillator and signal-crossover exits (RSI / Stochastic / %R / CCI / MFI / PPO / TRIX) have no intrinsic price level; the faithful exit is an oscillator condition, so the tuned stop is a risk floor, not a canonical target.
    • nr7_breakout session hold — Crabel's one-session (one-day) intraday hold has no exact analogue on a 24/7 market; the lookback-relative 10-bar stall-cut is the best available proxy. This is the only residual limit on NR7 — the narrowest-of-7-bars window itself is a fixable feature-timeframe defect (§13.B), not a compromise.

    13.D Choices that approximate a canon which does not map cleanly to 24/7 5m crypto

    • Long horizons via the daily bucket — the momentum/cross-asset canons run on weeks-to-months; the engine reads daily-bar returns (roc 90/180/365) aligned onto the 5m grid to represent 3/6/12-month horizons while the base timeframe stays 5m.
    • Volatility-target fraction 0.005 — set so equal-volatility sizing starts level with the existing risk-based behaviour given the 4·ATR stop (0.02 risk / 4 ATR), a neutral starting point rather than an invented target.
    • Per-lookback stall cuts — where a stall cut is kept, it is a multiple of the strategy's own window (target window, band period, breakout lookback) so it scales per symbol/timeframe instead of a fixed bar count.
    • year = 365 days — crypto trades 24/7, so annualisation and daily-bar horizons use 365, not the 252 trading-day equities convention.

    13.E What remains

    • Apply the pending code changes in §13.B once approved (the pivot stop swap, the oscillator exits, the feature-timeframe fixes, and the missing canonical terms).
    • Build the daily higher-timeframe feature columns §13.B / §10.3 require (daily high/low channel, narrowest-range flag, directional-bar count, inside-bar pattern, BandWidth-percentile, momentum-histogram).
    • Re-run the rule_lab_catalog_2024_SLIP_v2 campaign with the updated strategies and regenerate its reports.
    • Optionally wire the decision-cadence gate (§10.4).
